title: lore agents --check override read: harden settings read, boolean precedence, repo root, test gaps (post-merge review of #678)
description: Follow-up to the post-merge Opus review of #678 (LCLI-765, verdict recorded verbatim on that task), findings 1-4, all non-blocking. Filed only; implementation waits for a plan slot. lore-cli release stays held regardless. (1) disablesPlugin in src/core/agent-plugins.ts readFileSync follows a symlink to a FIFO or /dev/zero and can hang or exhaust lore: stat it, require isFile, cap the size. (2) the precedence walk stops on the first file that sets false, not the first file that sets a boolean for the key; latent in lore, but quest-cli#679 has the same defect as a blocking finding, so align the two. (3) the settings files are read from the process cwd, not the repository root, so a run from a subdirectory misses a root override and falls back to the old --scope user remedy; first measure whether Claude Code itself reads .claude/settings*.json from cwd or walks up. (4) four test gaps: a present-skill-file control for the reachability note, a synced row, a disabled local- or project-scope install row with an override file (must stay unchanged), and an init test with an override file (init.ts passes options.root at two call sites). Also unverified in the review and worth measuring here: that enable --scope project actually flips a user-installed plugin disabled by .claude/settings.json.

acceptanceCriteria.text: disablesPlugin never blocks or exhausts memory on a symlink to a FIFO or /dev/zero: a non-regular file or an oversized file means no override (proved with a FIFO fixture and a size-cap fixture, and both fail on the old code)
the override walk stops at the first settings file whose value for the plugin id is a boolean, so local true over project false names no override (proved both ways)
the settings files are read from the same directory the plugin listing is run in, or the cwd behaviour is measured and documented as intended

tests exist for a present-skill-file control, a synced row, a disabled local- or project-scope install row with an override file, and init with an override file, each failing on a mutant that removes the matching code

The plugin-claude-override line reads: plugin-claude-override <file> (<scope> scope) sets <plugin> to disabled, and is the effective setting in this checkout, with no precedence claim, and it is printed before the remedy in --plain (DEC-238 a9 items 5-6)

A disabling row in the committed .claude/settings.json gets the remedy claude plugin enable <plugin> --scope local (this machine only), the line says the project file disables it for every collaborator, a local override gets --scope local, a user-scope disable gets --scope user, and a managed row gets no command and says an administrator's managed setting disables it (DEC-238 a9 item 7; proved with a fixture per case)
lore never executes a settings-writing remedy: no code path runs claude plugin enable (proved by a test that the plugin port exposes no enable and the run records no enable invocation)

For the committed .claude/settings.json (project scope) row only, the override line is byte-identical to quest-cli QCLI-532: plugin-claude-override .claude/settings.json (project scope) sets opum-lore@opum to disabled for every collaborator, and is the effective setting in this checkout; every other row keeps the (a9) line unchanged (DEC-238 a10; proved with a fixture per row)

A DISABLED managed row prints no command and exactly "an administrator's managed setting disables it", while an INSTALLED managed row keeps the earlier agreed MANAGED_SCOPE_REMEDY, so the text is byte-identical to quest-cli on both rows (DEC-238 a9 item 7, Opus re-review of quest-cli#679 finding 1; proved both ways with a disabled and an installed managed fixture, and a mutant restoring the single remedy for both states fails)

implementationNotes: DEC-238 (a9), opum-doc 2026-10-25T14:10Z (record opum-ai/opum-doc#1369), relayed by the leader, recorded as NEW SCOPE for this task; waits for a plan slot, release held. Verbatim: "WORDING, DEC-238 (a9): 5. Both CLIs print the override line BEFORE the remedy in --plain (lore order); quest moves. 6. The line becomes `plugin-claude-override <file> (<scope> scope) sets <plugin> to disabled, and is the effective setting in this checkout`, with no precedence claim. (a6) is amended. 7. Amending (a6): a disabling row in the COMMITTED .claude/settings.json gets the remedy `claude plugin enable <plugin> --scope local` (this machine only, since local outranks project), and the line says the project file disables it for every collaborator. Local gets --scope local, user gets --scope user, and a managed row gets no command (\"an administrator's managed setting disables it\"). And neither CLI EXECUTES a settings-writing remedy without an explicit user command." Impact on lore as shipped in #678: item 5 already holds (override line precedes remedy); items 6 and 7 change the override sentence in src/core/agent-plugins.ts (overrideSentence) and move the project-scope remedy from --scope project to --scope local. Checked 2026-10-25 by grep: lore never executes claude plugin enable; enable appears only inside remedy strings (src/core/agent-plugins.ts remedyFor and withClaudeSettingsOverride), and AgentPluginPort exposes list and update only (update runs only for an installed, non-managed row). DEC-182 (1): this is settings code, so a Sonnet-or-above author and an Opus review before landing.

DEC-238 (a10), recorded in opum-ai/opum-doc#1371, relayed by the leader 2026-10-25; fixes the collaborator clause of (a9) item 7. Verbatim: "the collaborator clause goes inside the one line, for the project-file row only. Byte-identical in quest-cli (QCLI-532) and lore-cli (LCLI-766): `plugin-claude-override .claude/settings.json (project scope) sets <plugin> to disabled for every collaborator, and is the effective setting in this checkout` Every other row keeps (a9)'s line unchanged." So the separate "line says the project file disables it for every collaborator" wording in the (a9) criterion is now this one-line form. Implementation waits for a plan slot; release held.

Cross-CLI note 2026-10-25 from the Opus re-review of quest-cli#679, finding 1, relayed by the leader: quest now splits the managed remedy under DEC-238 (a9) item 7 - a DISABLED managed row prints no command and exactly "an administrator's managed setting disables it"; an INSTALLED managed row keeps the earlier agreed managed-scope remedy, because "disables it" would be false there. Lore as shipped has ONE constant for both states (src/core/agent-plugins.ts MANAGED_SCOPE_REMEDY, used in remedyFor for disabled and installed alike), so the pair is not byte-identical on the disabled managed row until this task makes the same split. Criterion added; implementation waits for a plan slot; release held.
